proofs.proof_tex:
Fix \(P\in\mathcal P_n\) and condition on \((M,\Omega)\).  Since \(\Omega\) is deterministic by \(\mathrm{ass:deterministic\mbox{-}mask}\), conditioning on \((M,\Omega)\) does not alter any of the conditional independence or moment assertions given \(M\).  For \((j,u)\in I\times J\), define
\[
 X_{ju}=s^{-1}w_{ju}\epsilon_{ju}.
\]
The weights and \(s\) are fixed under this conditioning by \(\mathrm{def:oracle\mbox{-}score\mbox{-}variance}\).  By \(\mathrm{ass:centered\mbox{-}noise}\),
\[
 \mathbb E_P[X_{ju}\mid M,\Omega]
 =s^{-1}w_{ju}\mathbb E_P[\epsilon_{ju}\mid M]=0.
\]

We next verify finite-range dependence rather than assume a central limit theorem.  Equip \(I\times J\subset\mathbb Z_+^2\) with the maximum metric.  Consider two collections of indices whose mutual distance is greater than \(q\).  Coordinates belonging to distinct rows generate conditionally independent sigma-fields by \(\mathrm{ass:independent\mbox{-}rows}\).  Within any common row, the corresponding time sets are separated by more than \(q\), so their sigma-fields are conditionally independent by \(\mathrm{ass:conditional\mbox{-}block\mbox{-}dependence}\).  Factoring over rows shows that the two full collections are conditionally independent.  Thus \(\{X_{ju}:(j,u)\in I\times J\}\) is a conditionally \(q\)-dependent random field.  If \(q=0\), it is also conditionally one-dependent, so below one may take \(k_0=\max\{q,1\}\).

Conditional row independence makes cross-row covariances vanish.  Within a row, conditional block dependence and conditional centering make covariances vanish at lags \(|h|>q\), while \(\mathrm{ass:common\mbox{-}stationary\mbox{-}covariance}\) gives covariance \(\gamma(h)\) at lag \(h\).  With the convention \(w_{j,u}=0\) outside \(J\), \(\mathrm{def:oracle\mbox{-}score\mbox{-}variance}\) therefore yields
\[
\begin{aligned}
 \operatorname{Var}_P\!\left(\sum_{j=1}^N\sum_{u=1}^T X_{ju}\middle|M,\Omega\right)
 &=\frac{1}{s^2}\sum_{j=1}^N\sum_{h=-q}^{q}\gamma(h)
     \sum_{u=1}^T w_{ju}w_{j,u+h}\\
 &=\frac{s^2}{s^2}=1.
\end{aligned}
\]
Division by \(s\) is valid because \(s^2\ge c_s/(nH)>0\) by \(\mathrm{ass:variance\mbox{-}nondegeneracy}\).

The conditional exponential-moment condition supplies the moment premise of the cited normal-approximation lemma.  Indeed, for an absolute numerical constant \(C_3<\infty\), the elementary bound
\[
 |x|^3\le C_3K^3\exp(x^2/K^2),\qquad x\in\mathbb R,
\]
and \(\mathrm{ass:conditional\mbox{-}subgaussian\mbox{-}noise}\) imply, almost surely,
\[
 \sup_{j,u}\mathbb E_P[|\epsilon_{ju}|^3\mid M,\Omega]
 \le 2C_3K^3.
\]
Apply \(\mathrm{lem:chen\mbox{-}shao\mbox{-}finite\mbox{-}range\mbox{-}normal\mbox{-}bound}\) conditionally, with \(p_0=3\), \(d_0=2\), \(k_0=\max\{q,1\}\), and index set \(I\times J\).  Since \(\sum_{j,u}X_{ju}=L/s\), the preceding centering, dependence, moment, and unit-variance calculations verify all of its premises.  Consequently,
\[
\begin{aligned}
 &\sup_{z\in\mathbb R}
 \left|\mathbb P_P\!\left(\frac{L}{s}\le z\middle|M,\Omega\right)-\Phi(z)\right|\\
 &\quad\le
 75(10k_0+1)^4\sum_{j=1}^N\sum_{u=1}^T
 \mathbb E_P[|X_{ju}|^3\mid M,\Omega]\\
 &\quad\le C_qK^3s^{-3}\sum_{j=1}^N\sum_{u=1}^T|w_{ju}|^3\\
 &\quad\le C_qK^3
 \left(s^{-1}\max_{j,u}|w_{ju}|\right)
 \left(s^{-2}\sum_{j,u}w_{ju}^2\right).
\end{aligned}
\]
By the already established \(\mathrm{lem:score\mbox{-}diffuseness}\), the first factor in the last line is \(o(1)\) uniformly over \(P\in\mathcal P_n\), and the second is \(O(1)\) uniformly over that class.  The constants \(q\) and \(K\) are fixed by \(\mathrm{ass:fixed\mbox{-}known\mbox{-}range}\) and \(\mathrm{ass:conditional\mbox{-}subgaussian\mbox{-}noise}\).  Taking the supremum over \(P\in\mathcal P_n\) in the displayed bound proves
\[
 \sup_{P\in\mathcal P_n}\sup_{z\in\mathbb R}
 \left|\mathbb P_P\!\left(\frac{L}{s}\le z\middle|M,\Omega\right)-\Phi(z)\right|
 \longrightarrow0,
\]
which is the claimed uniform conditional central limit theorem.

open_obligations.what_is_open: Prove a simultaneous active-rank neighborhood and a uniform second-order expansion for every implemented masked nuclear-norm fixed point, then control the centered quadratic aggregate, cubic and regularization terms, pretreatment reconstruction, fitted curvature, and fitted influence weights at the theorem's stated rates.
open_obligations.obstruction: The exact proximal identity is a nonsmooth self-consistency equation. The frozen assumptions and established local differential do not furnish a contraction for its missing-coordinate fixed point or a uniform spectral gap for all native fits. Even pointwise smoothness would not control the signed aggregate because the local fits reuse the same donor and pretreatment observations. Proximal nonexpansiveness alone loses that averaging gain and does not imply the displayed curvature or relative-weight rates.
open_obligations.attempted: The implemented optimizer was reduced to its exact singular-value-thresholding fixed point; the complete three-block differential and target-coordinate auxiliary separation were retained. The asserted raw rates were converted exactly to the oracle standard-error scale, including the residual-covariance term. A direct Lipschitz or nonexpansive comparison remains too coarse, while treating the unpenalized smooth branch as the native optimizer would assume the missing crux.

open_obligations.what_is_open: Derive the native masked-optimizer and fitted-correction rates needed for the proposition's final assertion that the corrected aggregate remainder is little-o at the inverse-panel scale.
open_obligations.obstruction: The rank-one Hessian contraction proves the oracle quadratic drift, including its parity constants, but it does not establish that the nonsmooth masked optimizer follows the same expansion uniformly or that the fitted curvature correction is accurate at the inverse-panel scale. Those statements are exactly the unresolved content of the native second-order transfer theorem.
open_obligations.attempted: The local singular-value ratio, complete three-term derivative, exact serial quadratic contraction, parity average, model-class checks, and rate substitution for a proportional window and signal exponent four fifths were carried out. Proximal nonexpansiveness leaves a bound larger than the inverse-panel scale, so it cannot certify the early kill test.
open_obligations.partial_result:
For the declared calibration, restriction of the normalized constant left factor to \(I_{it}=C(t)\cup\{i\}\) has squared norm \(3/4+1/n\).  Restriction of the normalized alternating right factor to \(J_{it}=S\cup\{t\}\) has squared norm \(1/2+4p_t^2/(5n)\).  Since the signal is rank one, multiplication of these two restricted norms gives the exact identity
\[
 \frac{\psi_{\mathrm{loc},it}}{\psi}
 =\sqrt{\left(\frac34+\frac1n\right)
 \left(\frac12+\frac{4p_t^2}{5n}\right)}
 \longrightarrow\sqrt{\frac38}>\frac12=c_{\mathrm{loc}}.
\]
The completed first-order perturbation inserted into the exact rank-one projector Hessian yields the already calculated covariance contraction
\[
 \psi_{\mathrm{loc},it}\,
 \mathbb E\!\left[
 q_{it}\!\left(P_{\Omega_{\mathrm{loc}}^{it}}R_{it}\epsilon\right)
 \middle|M\right]
 =-\frac{6\sqrt{3/2}}{5\sqrt5}\,p_t+O(n^{-1}).
\]
Combining it with the preceding local-to-global singular-value ratio gives, for each fixed parity,
\[
 \psi\,
 \mathbb E\!\left[
 q_{it}\!\left(P_{\Omega_{\mathrm{loc}}^{it}}R_{it}\epsilon\right)
 \middle|M\right]
 \longrightarrow-\frac{12p_t}{5\sqrt5}.
\]
Thus the even and odd limits are \(-18/(5\sqrt5)\) and \(-6/(5\sqrt5)\).  The declared consecutive window has equally many indices of each parity, so
\[
 \psi B_2\longrightarrow-\frac{12}{5\sqrt5}.
\]

The remaining assertion is exactly conditional on the unresolved native-transfer rates.  Put
\[
 \mathcal R_n=\frac1{gH}\sum_{i\in G,t\in W}(\widehat M_{it}-M_{it})-L-\widehat B_2.
\]
The decomposition in the native-transfer target would give
\[
 |\mathcal R_n|\le |Q-B_2|+|R_{\mathrm{agg}}|+|\widehat B_2-B_2|.
\]
Here \(H\asymp n\), \(m\asymp n\), \(\psi=n^{4/5}\), \(\psi_{\min,\mathrm{loc}}\ge\psi/2\), and the asserted pretreatment rate would give \(\Delta_\gamma=O_{\mathbb P}(\ell_n^2n^{-1/2})\).  Direct substitution into the target's raw rates then gives
\[
\begin{aligned}
 n|\mathcal R_n|
 &=O_{\mathbb P}\!\left(
 \ell_n^4n^{-3/10}
 +\ell_n^4n^{-1/10}
 +\ell_n^4n^{-1/2}
 +\ell_n^2n^{-3/10}
 \right)\\
 &=o_{\mathbb P}(1).
\end{aligned}
\]
This proves the exponent arithmetic and the complete oracle drift calculation, but the native masked-optimizer and fitted-correction bounds used in the last implication remain precisely the unproved content of \(\mathrm{thm:native\mbox{-}second\mbox{-}order\mbox{-}transfer}\).

open_obligations.what_is_open: Establish the native expansion, feasible curvature rate, residual covariance rate, and relative fitted-weight consistency required before the proved oracle score limit can be studentized.
open_obligations.obstruction: The causal cancellation, banded-Toeplitz variance comparison, conditional Gaussian score limit, and coverage reduction are closed, but each remaining stochastic error is a conclusion of the unresolved native-transfer theorem. Using those conclusions now would make this theorem depend on an unproved target rather than on the frozen primitives.
open_obligations.attempted: The exact causal error identity was combined with the native theorem's proposed decomposition. Variance consistency was reduced by an explicit quadratic-form expansion to covariance consistency and relative fitted-weight consistency. The conditional score central limit theorem was proved directly from the cited finite-range normal bound.
open_obligations.partial_result:
The causal reduction is exact.  On \(G\times W\), \(\mathrm{ass:common\mbox{-}start\mbox{-}mask}\) gives \(A_{it}=1\), and \(\mathrm{ass:causal\mbox{-}consistency}\) therefore gives \(Y^{\mathrm{obs}}_{it}=Y_{it}(1)\).  Comparing the definitions of \(\widehat\tau\) and \(\tau\) yields
\[
 \widehat\tau-\tau
 =-\frac1{gH}\sum_{i\in G,t\in W}(\widehat M_{it}-M_{it}).
\]
Consequently, if \(\mathrm{thm:native\mbox{-}second\mbox{-}order\mbox{-}transfer}\) were established, its decomposition and \(\widehat\tau_{\mathrm{bc}}=\widehat\tau+\widehat B_2\) would give
\[
\begin{aligned}
 \widehat\tau_{\mathrm{bc}}-\tau
 &=-L-Q-R_{\mathrm{agg}}+\widehat B_2\\
 &=-L-(Q-B_2)-R_{\mathrm{agg}}+(\widehat B_2-B_2)\\
 &=-L+o_{\mathbb P}(s),
\end{aligned}
\]
where the final equality follows from the standard-error calculations recorded for the native-transfer target.

For the studentization reduction, let \(d=\widehat w-w\), and let \(\Gamma_q\) and \(\widehat\Gamma_q\) be the \(T\times T\) banded Toeplitz matrices whose \((u,v)\) entries are \(1\{|u-v|\le q\}\gamma(v-u)\) and \(1\{|u-v|\le q\}\widehat\gamma(v-u)\), respectively.  By the definitions of \(s^2\) and \(\widehat V\),
\[
 s^2=\sum_{j=1}^N w_{j\cdot}^{\top}\Gamma_qw_{j\cdot},
 \qquad
 \widehat V=\sum_{j=1}^N(w_{j\cdot}+d_{j\cdot})^{\top}
 \widehat\Gamma_q(w_{j\cdot}+d_{j\cdot}).
\]
Fixed \(q\), the conditional moment bound, and \(\Delta_\gamma=o_{\mathbb P}(1)\) imply
\[
 \|\widehat\Gamma_q\|_{\mathrm{op}}=O_{\mathbb P}(1),
 \qquad
 \|\widehat\Gamma_q-\Gamma_q\|_{\mathrm{op}}
 \le(2q+1)\Delta_\gamma=o_{\mathbb P}(1).
\]
Expanding the two quadratic forms and applying Cauchy--Schwarz therefore gives
\[
\begin{aligned}
 |\widehat V-s^2|
 &\le \|\widehat\Gamma_q\|_{\mathrm{op}}
 \left(2\|w\|_F\|d\|_F+\|d\|_F^2\right)
 +\|\widehat\Gamma_q-\Gamma_q\|_{\mathrm{op}}\|w\|_F^2\\
 &=O_{\mathbb P}\!\left(
 \|w\|_F\|d\|_F+\|d\|_F^2+\Delta_\gamma\|w\|_F^2
 \right).
\end{aligned}
\]
The established score-diffuseness result gives \(\|w\|_F^2=O(s^2)\).  Hence the native-transfer conclusions \(\|d\|_F^2=o_{\mathbb P}(s^2)\) and \(\Delta_\gamma=o_{\mathbb P}(1)\) would imply
\[
 \frac{|\widehat V-s^2|}{s^2}
 =O_{\mathbb P}\!\left(
 \frac{\|w\|_F}{s}\frac{\|d\|_F}{s}
 +\frac{\|d\|_F^2}{s^2}+\Delta_\gamma\frac{\|w\|_F^2}{s^2}
 \right)=o_{\mathbb P}(1).
\]
The conditional score central limit theorem is proved in this dispatch.  Once the unresolved native-transfer inputs are available, conditional Slutsky applied to the last two displays yields the claimed studentized normal limit.  Since \(z_{1-\alpha/2}\) is finite for fixed \(\alpha\in(0,1)\), evaluation at its two continuity points gives conditional coverage tending uniformly to \(1-\alpha\).  Thus the causal identity, variance comparison, score limit, and final coverage implication are closed; the only missing premise is the estimator-specific native second-order transfer and its plug-in conclusions.

proofs.proof_tex:
Fix a compact set \(\mathcal K\subset[1/2,1]\times(0,1]\times[0,1]\), and put
\[
 b_*=\min\{b:(a,b,c)\in\mathcal K\}>0.
\]
All constants below are uniform over \((a,b,c)\in\mathcal K\) and \(P\in\mathcal P_n(a,b,c)\).  This uniformity follows because the constants in the cohort-growth, window-growth, and frontier-variance assumptions are locally uniform over compact exponent sets, while the constants in the balanced-growth, incoherence, and restricted-Gram assumptions are fixed.

We first retain the normalized-factor part of the already established result \(\mathrm{lem:score\mbox{-}diffuseness}\), which does not use the fixed-fraction cohort assumption.  For completeness, write
\[
 u_i=D^{-1/2}x_i,
 \qquad
 v_t=D^{-1/2}f_t.
\]
Because \(D\) is positive definite by exact rank, these vectors are well defined.  From \(X=UD^{1/2}\), \(F=VD^{1/2}\), incoherence, and balanced growth,
\[
 \max_{i\in I}\lVert u_i\rVert_2
 \le \sqrt{\frac{\mu r}{N}}
 \le Cn^{-1/2},
 \qquad
 \max_{t\in J}\lVert v_t\rVert_2
 \le \sqrt{\frac{\mu r}{T}}
 \le Cn^{-1/2}.
\]
Moreover, the normalized donor and preperiod Gram bounds give
\[
 \sum_{j\in C(t)}u_ju_j^{\top}\succeq c_AI_r,
 \qquad
 \sum_{s\in S}v_sv_s^{\top}\succeq c_BI_r.
\]
Thus both matrices are invertible.  Defining the donor and preperiod tangent coefficients by
\[
 a_{ij,t}
 =u_i^{\top}\!\left(\sum_{k\in C(t)}u_ku_k^{\top}\right)^{-1}u_j,
 \qquad
 b_{t,s}
 =v_t^{\top}\!\left(\sum_{u\in S}v_uv_u^{\top}\right)^{-1}v_s,
\]
Cauchy--Schwarz and the two inverse bounds yield
\[
 \sup_{i\in G,\,t\in W,\,j\in C(t)}|a_{ij,t}|\le \frac{C}{n},
 \qquad
 \sup_{t\in W,\,s\in S}|b_{t,s}|\le \frac{C}{n}.
\]

Let \(\mathcal D=I\setminus G\).  Under the common-start design, \(C(t)=\mathcal D\) for every \(t\in W\).  Expanding the same complete three-term tangent score used in \(\mathrm{lem:score\mbox{-}diffuseness}\) inside the definition of \(L\), the coefficient of each noise coordinate is
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 w^{(1)}_{jt}
 &=\frac{1}{gH}\sum_{i\in G}a_{ij,t},
 &&(j,t)\in\mathcal D\times W,\\
 w^{(2)}_{is}
 &=\frac{1}{gH}\sum_{t\in W}b_{t,s},
 &&(i,s)\in G\times S,\\
 w^{(3)}_{js}
 &=-\frac{1}{gH}\sum_{i\in G}\sum_{t\in W}a_{ij,t}b_{t,s},
 &&(j,s)\in\mathcal D\times S.
 \end{aligned}
\]
The three supports are pairwise disjoint: \(G\cap\mathcal D=\varnothing\), and \(S\cap W=\varnothing\) follows from \(\max S<\min W\).  The coefficient bounds therefore imply
\[
 \max_{j\in I,\,s'\in J}|w_{js'}|
 \le C\max\left\{\frac{1}{nH},\frac{1}{ng},\frac{1}{n^2}\right\}.
\]
Balanced growth and \(S\subset J\) show that the three support cardinalities are at most \(CnH\), \(Cgn\), and \(Cn^2\), respectively.  Consequently,
\[
 \sum_{j\in I}\sum_{s'\in J}w_{js'}^2
 =\sum_{\mathcal D\times W}(w^{(1)}_{jt})^2
  +\sum_{G\times S}(w^{(2)}_{is})^2
  +\sum_{\mathcal D\times S}(w^{(3)}_{js})^2
 \le C\left\{\frac{1}{nH}+\frac{1}{ng}+\frac{1}{n^2}\right\}.
\]

Set
\[
 A_n=\frac{1}{nH},
 \qquad
 B_n=\frac{1}{ng}.
\]
The frontier variance-scale assumption supplies the strictly positive lower bound
\[
 s^2\ge c_v(A_n+B_n).
\]
The window-growth assumption and \(c\le1\) give \(H\le Cn^c\le Cn\), whence \(n^{-2}\le CA_n\).  Division by the preceding positive variance bound is therefore legitimate and gives
\[
 s^{-2}\sum_{j\in I}\sum_{s'\in J}w_{js'}^2
 \le C\frac{A_n+B_n+n^{-2}}{A_n+B_n}
 \le C.
\]

For the maximal weight, \(s\ge c\sqrt{A_n+B_n}\) implies separately
\[
 \frac{A_n}{s}\le C\sqrt{A_n},
 \qquad
 \frac{B_n}{s}\le C\sqrt{B_n},
 \qquad
 \frac{n^{-2}}{s}
 \le C\frac{n^{-2}}{\sqrt{A_n}}
 =C\frac{\sqrt{nH}}{n^2}
 \le \frac{C}{n}.
\]
Since \(H\ge c_Hn^c\ge c_H\) and \(g\ge c_gn^b\ge c_gn^{b_*}\) uniformly on \(\mathcal K\), it follows that
\[
 \sup_{(a,b,c)\in\mathcal K}\sup_{P\in\mathcal P_n(a,b,c)}
 \frac{\max_{j\in I,\,s'\in J}|w_{js'}|}{s}
 \le C\left\{n^{-1/2}+n^{-(1+b_*)/2}+n^{-1}\right\}
 \longrightarrow0.
\]
Together with the preceding uniform squared-weight bound, this proves both asserted diffuseness conclusions.
